leftEvidence.title: God and Mammon cannot both be served

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus states that no one can serve two masters.
points.right: Jesus repeats the warning against anxious questions about necessities and contrasts the nations’ seeking with the Father’s knowledge.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Love and hate, devotion and contempt expose the division between God and Mammon.
points.right: The hearers are told to seek God’s Kingdom and righteousness first and to leave tomorrow’s trouble to tomorrow.

payload.posture: Exclusive service to God is followed by first seeking God’s Kingdom and righteousness.

rightEvidence.title: Kingdom seeking is placed before tomorrow

payload.tension: Seeking first does not answer every practical question about possession and provision.
payload.title: What is served and what is sought first
